seoDescription: Learn how to build a dynamic, professional image slideshow in Drupal 7 using the Views module. This comprehensive tutorial walks you through creating a custom content type for your slides, configuring image styles to automatically scale and crop your pictures, and installing the necessary modules like Views Slideshow and the jQuery Cycle plugin. You'll master the step-by-step process of building the View, adding fields, configuring filters for unpublished content, and setting up an interactive pager.

chapters.title: Introduction & Project Goal
chapters.description: This chapter introduces the goal of creating a Drupal 7 slideshow and demonstrates the features of the final product.

chapters.title: Creating the Slideshow Content Type
chapters.description: Learn to create a dedicated content type for slideshow images, including why it's best to keep these nodes unpublished.

chapters.title: Configuring Content Type Fields
chapters.description: This chapter covers adding and configuring the required fields for the new content type, including the image field and display settings.

chapters.title: Adding and Customizing the Image Field
chapters.description: This section details how to add the image field, set it as required, organize its file directory, and adjust its display settings.

chapters.title: Managing Display and Adding Content
chapters.description: Adjust the manage display settings for better previews and then begin adding image content to the new slideshow content type.

chapters.title: Creating a Custom Image Style
chapters.description: Walk through creating a custom Drupal image style to automatically scale and crop uploaded slideshow images to the correct dimensions.

chapters.title: Module and Library Installation
chapters.description: This chapter covers downloading and setting up the required modules (Views, CTools, Views Slideshow) and the essential jQuery Cycle library.

chapters.title: Creating the Slideshow View
chapters.description: Begin building the slideshow by creating a new View, defining its page path, and setting the display format to 'Slideshow'.

chapters.title: Configuring View Filters and Settings
chapters.description: Adjust the View to display unpublished content and configure the core slideshow settings like transition effects and hover behavior.

chapters.title: Setting Up the Pager Controls
chapters.description: Learn how to create a numeric pager for the slideshow by adding and configuring a 'Global: View result counter' field in Views.

chapters.title: Final Steps and Next Steps
chapters.description: Set the new View as the site's front page, review the functional slideshow, and learn what will be covered in the next tutorial on CSS styling.

summary:
## Project Goal

Create a dynamic, front-page image slideshow in **Drupal 7** using the **Views** module. The final product will feature automatically rotating images, a text overlay for the title, a pager for navigation, and a pause-on-hover effect.

## Content Structure

To manage the slideshow images, a new **Content Type** is created with specific settings:

-   **Name**: `Front page slideshow`.
-   **Fields**: The default `body` field is removed, leaving only the `Title` and a new `Image` field (`slideshow image`).
-   **Published Status**: Nodes of this type are created as **unpublished** by default. This prevents individual slide images from appearing as separate, findable pages on the site, as they are only meant to be displayed within the slideshow view.

## Image Handling with Image Styles

To ensure all slideshow images have consistent dimensions, a custom **Image Style** is created. This avoids manual image editing and allows Drupal to handle resizing automatically.

1.  **Scale**: First, an effect is added to **scale** all images to a specific width (e.g., `700px`) while maintaining the aspect ratio.
2.  **Crop**: Next, an effect is added to **crop** the scaled image to the final height (e.g., `200px`), anchored to the center to control the focal point.

> [!NOTE]
> Using Drupal's Image Styles is fast and automatic, but you have less control over the final cropping. Manually pre-sizing images takes more time but gives you full control over the composition.

## Required Modules & Libraries

This project requires several key components:

-   **Drupal Modules**:
    -   `Views`
    -   `Chaos Tools` (ctools)
    -   `Views Slideshow` (which includes `Views Slideshow: Cycle`)
    -   `Libraries API`
-   **JavaScript Library**: The `Views Slideshow` module depends on the **jQuery Cycle plugin**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> ### jQuery Cycle Plugin Installation
> 1.  Download the plugin from the link provided on the Views Slideshow project page (get the `...min.js` file).
> 2.  Create a directory path: `sites/all/libraries/jquery.cycle/`.
> 3.  **Rename** the downloaded file to `jquery.cycle.all.min.js`.
> 4.  Place the renamed file inside the `jquery.cycle` directory.

## Views Configuration

 The slideshow is built using a **View** with the following key configurations:

-   **Basic Setup**: Create a new **Page** display showing **Content** of the `Front page slideshow` type.
-   **Format**: Set the format to **Slideshow** and the `Show` option to **Fields**.
-   **Filters**: **Remove** the default `Content: Published (Yes)` filter to ensure your unpublished slide nodes are displayed.
-   **Fields**:
    1.  `Content: Slideshow image`: The main image field. Set its **Formatter** to use the custom **Image Style** (`banner style`) you created.
    2.  `Content: Title`: The title of the slide.
    3.  `Global: View result counter`: This field is added to generate numbers for the pager.
        -   **Crucially, check `Exclude from display` for this field.**
-   **Pager Setup**: In the `Format: Slideshow` **settings**, under **Pager**, select the `Global: View result counter` field as the `Pager fields`.
-   **Slideshow Behavior**: Also in the format settings, choose a `Cycle` **effect** (e.g., `fade`) and enable **`Pause on hover`**.

## Final Steps & Next Steps

1.  **Set Front Page**: Navigate to `Configuration > Site information` and set the `Default front page` to the path of your new View (e.g., `home`).
2.  **Styling**: The created View provides a functional but unstyled slideshow. The next step, covered in the following tutorial, is to use **CSS** to style the pager and overlay the title onto the image.
